title: The first impression trap
topic: why your boss never forgets a first impression
hook: Two new hires. The same work. But the boss has already decided who is better.

cast.description: Sam, a young new hire who starts his first day badly but works well.
The boss, a woman around fifty who judges the new hires.
Nora, the other new hire, who does the same work.

promise: The first thing we see about someone becomes the lens for everything they do after (the primacy effect).

takeaway.text: Before you judge someone, ask: what would I think if this were their first day?

scenes.narration: Two new hires. The same work. But the boss has already decided who is better.
scenes.visualIdea: Close on the boss, judging, then she has decided.

scenes.narration: Day one. Sam walks into his interview a little late, hands over a crumpled CV, and sits down.
scenes.visualIdea: Sam enters the boss's office, sits, hands over his CV.
scenes.action: Sam walks in late and hands over his CV.

scenes.narration: In the first ten seconds, the boss reads it, frowns, and types one word. Careless.
scenes.visualIdea: The boss reads, frowns and types.

scenes.narration: Then Sam answers every question well. Clear, calm, smart.
But later, the boss thinks it over. Good answers? He probably memorised them.
Psychologists call it the primacy effect. What we see first becomes the lens for everything after.
scenes.visualIdea: Sam and Nora side by side, a balance scale tips toward Nora although they did the same.

scenes.narration: Six months later, the same results. Nora gets the praise. Sam gets the doubt.
So before you judge someone, ask: what would I think if this were their first day?
scenes.visualIdea: The boss thinks, then sees it.
